chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cycles of prayer after Maghrib on the night of Muzdalifa, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Pray them after Isha, four cycles.'
ai.seo_question: How many voluntary prayer cycles should be performed after Isha on the night of Muzdalifa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific practice for the night of Muzdalifa, prescribing four voluntary rak'at to be performed after the Isha prayer. This ruling highlights the distinct spiritual status of Muzdalifa as a time for devotion separate from the main rituals of Arafat and Mina, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to the Imams' guidance in Hajj jurisprudence. The instruction underscores the importance of integrating personal worship with the communal rites of pilgrimage.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Anbasa Bin Mus’ab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the (Prayer) Cycles which are (to be Prayed) after Al-Maghrib on the night of Al-Muzdalifa. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Pray these after Al-Isha, four Cycles’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Muskan from ‘Anbasah ibn Mus’ab who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the Rak‘ats of Salat (prayer) after al-Maghrib during the night of al-Muzdalifah. He (the Imam) said, ‘Perform them after al-‘Isha’ as four Rak‘at.’”
